newsitem.title: USA: NY judge orders NYC to assess workfare - paper.
newsitem.headline: NY judge orders NYC to assess workfare - paper.

text.p: A New York State Supreme Court justice told New York City it must stop assigning welfare recipients to workfare unless it first fully assesses their needs and skills to see if instead an education program is more appropriate, the New York Times said on Wednesday.

Acting Justice Janis Solomon of State Supreme Court in Manhattan issued an injunction on Monday after making a preliminary finding that the Giuliani Administration was violating state law by sending many of its welfare recipients to its Work Experience Program without doing proper individual assessments, the paper said.

Six welfare recipients had sued the city, which had steered them into its 35,000-person workfare program, saying it was hurting their chances for jobs and economic advancement by not evaluating their needs and directing them away from education.
City officials say that putting welfare recipients into workfare jobs is the best route for permanent employment, the New York Times said.

The justice asked the plantiffs' lawyers to draft an order to tell the city exactly what it had to do to satisfy the rquirements on individual assessments called for by state law. The city then would respond to the proposed order, and the justice would issue the formal order, probably next month.
The paper quoted the city's Corporation Counsel, Paul Crotty, as saying it was highly unlikely that the city would appeal the order, though his office said the city is in compliance with the law.
